London, 23<sup>rd</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Platinum jewellery demand** in China, a key consumer, is likely to weather the current economic slump more robustly than in Japan, another top market, said James Courage, chief executive of Platinum Guild International. The strength of the Chinese market is due to the relatively healthy state of its economy, he said, noting that China and Japan represent about 75 % of total consumer demand for platinum jewellery. “On the economic side, they (China) haven’t seen the same degree of downturn,” he said. “Also as a share of the jewellery market, platinum has perhaps a greater share of the total market in China than it does in Japan.” Courage said the bridal market, which is a key sector for both Asian countries, remained relatively protected from a deterioration in the economy.  Courage said that the sharp decline in price meant that the level of recycling has come down significantly from a few years ago, which represented an opportunity for new metals sales in the market this year. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Toyota** is considering cutting full-time employees in North America and the UK, a company source familiar with the matter said.  It is cutting production as the global financial crisis sends sales plummeting and puts the carmaker on course for its first ever operating loss in the year to March. Its U.S. sales in December fell 37%.  The Japanese business daily _Nikkei_ said Toyota was considering cutting up to 1,000 full-time jobs in North America and Britain, as shoppers stop buying cars and the pressure to cut fixed costs mounts.  Toyota is considering going beyond cutting temporary and contract staff to easing out regular employees in North America and the UK.  The decision on job reductions and possible pay cuts would likely be made as early as next week. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**U.S. sales of gasoline-electric hybrids** fell 9.9 % in 2008, after rising with gasoline prices early in the year and falling along with fuel costs and a collapsing auto market at the end.Automakers sold 315,761 hybrids last year, 2.4 % of the total vehicle market. Toyota U.S.A. again sold about three of every four hybrids in the United States, despite new entries from GM. The segment-leading Toyota Prius reflected the topsy-turvy year: it tallied 91,440 sales in H1 and 67,444 in H2.  “At $1.50 a gallon, the American public is not willing to pay for fuel-saving technology,” GM Vice Chairman Bob Lutz said.  American Honda Motor Co. and Toyota each sold 12.5 % fewer hybrids last year than in 2007. Ford, No. 3 in hybrid sales behind Honda, suffered the greatest decline, down 22.2 %. GM nearly tripled sales to 14,439 after adding hybrid versions of the Cadillac Escalade, GMC Yukon and Chevrolet Malibu and Tahoe.  Combined Detroit 3 hybrid sales were below Honda’s total of 31,495, and Honda sold one hybrid for every eight Toyota delivered. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Metix** has completed

work at the world’s third-largest platinum producer Lonmin’s plant, near Rustenburg.  Apart from having replaced the electrode systems on a six-in-line matte smelting furnace for Lonmin, Metix was also contracted to completely rebuild the existing furnace, including its linings and bus tubes.  “The project was valued at about R125-million and was completed in 12 months”. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**RBC said the PGM pricing basket** is expected to underperform throughout 2009 or until the economy and automotive sector make a sustainable recovery in late 2009 or early 2010. _Source:  Mineweb_ 

**AU Optronics** has estimated a 15-20% drop in its large-size LCD panel shipments in the first quarter this year, with TV panel shipments remaining flat, and IT (monitor and notebook) panel shipments dropping 20%, according to company executive VP of global business unit Paul Peng. _Source: Digitimes_
